It has taken decades of scholarship to reveal the mechanism’s secrets and understand the
Greeks’ extensive knowledge of astronomy. The size of a shoebox, the device had plates
on the front and back framed by a wooden case enclosing about 60 gears. The front plate
had a circular dial with pointers tracking the movement of the sun, moon and five known

circling. The Greeks compensated for this through ingenious engineering that periodically
slowed the gears and reversed their rotation to control the orbits. The back plate was
similarly impressive. It had two large dials: one displayed a Greek lunar month calendar
while the other showed the two- and four-yearly cycles of athletic competitions, Including
the Olympics. A lever on one side of the device turned the gears to set the front and back
dials in motion.
